source_units.text: Empty and false hopes belong to a man without understanding, and dreams give wings to fools.
Like someone grasping a shadow and chasing wind is the one who relies on dreams.
A dream vision is this set against that, a likeness of a face opposite a face.
What will be cleansed from something unclean? What will prove true from something false?
Divinations, omens, and dreams are vain, and the heart imagines like a woman in labor.
Unless they are sent from the Most High in a visitation, do not give your heart to them.
For dreams have led many astray, and those who hoped in them fell away.
The law will be fulfilled without falsehood, and wisdom is fulfillment in a faithful mouth.
A man who has wandered has learned much, and one with much experience will recount understanding.
The one who has not been tested knows little, but the one who has wandered will increase in skill.
I have seen many things in my wandering, and my understanding exceeds my words.
Often I was in danger to the point of death, and because of these things I was preserved.
The spirit of those who fear the Lord will live, for their hope rests upon the One who saves them.
The one who fears the Lord will fear nothing and certainly not be cowardly, because He Himself is his hope.
Happy is the soul of the one who fears the Lord! On whom does he rely? Who is his support?
The Lord’s eyes are upon those who love Him: a mighty shield and strong support, shelter from scorching heat and shelter from midday, protection from stumbling and help against falling,
raising the soul and brightening the eyes, giving healing, life, and blessing.
One who sacrifices from unjust gain makes a blemished offering, and the gifts of the lawless bring no acceptance.
The Most High takes no pleasure in the offerings of the ungodly, nor does He atone for sins through a multitude of sacrifices.
The one who presents a sacrifice from the property of the poor is slaughtering a son before his father.
The bread of the needy is the life of the poor; the one who deprives them of it is a man of blood.
The one who takes away a livelihood murders his neighbor, and the one who withholds a hired worker’s wage sheds blood.
One builds and another tears down; what have they gained beyond toil?
One prays and another curses; whose voice will the Master hear?
Someone washes after contact with a corpse and then touches it again; what has he gained by his washing?
So is a person who fasts over his sins and goes again to do the same things. Who will hear his prayer, and what has he gained by humbling himself?
The one who keeps the law multiplies offerings; the one who attends to commandments sacrifices a peace offering.
The one who repays kindness offers fine flour, and the one who gives alms sacrifices a praise offering.
To withdraw from wickedness is the Lord’s good pleasure, and to withdraw from injustice is atonement.
Do not appear empty before the Lord, for all these things are for the commandment’s sake.
A righteous person’s offering fattens the altar, and its fragrance is before the Most High.
A righteous man’s sacrifice is acceptable, and its memorial will not be forgotten.
Glorify the Lord with a generous eye, and do not diminish the firstfruits of your hands.
With every gift make your face cheerful, and consecrate a tenth with gladness.
Give to the Most High according to His gift, with a generous eye according to what your hand has found.
For the Lord repays, and He will repay you sevenfold.
Do not bribe, for He will not accept it, and do not rely on an unjust sacrifice.
For the Lord is judge, and with Him there is no prestige of persons.
He will not show partiality against the poor, and He will hear the petition of the wronged.
He will certainly not disregard an orphan’s supplication or a widow when she pours out her words.
Do not a widow’s tears run down her cheek, and her cry rise against the one who brought them down?
The one who serves acceptably will be received, and his petition will reach as far as the clouds.
A humble person’s prayer has passed through the clouds, and until it draws near, he will certainly not be comforted.
He will certainly not withdraw until the Most High visits, judges in favor of the righteous, and executes judgment.
The Lord will certainly not delay or be patient with them,
until He crushes the loins of the merciless and repays the nations with retribution,
until He removes the multitude of the insolent and crushes the scepters of the unjust,
until He repays a person according to his actions and judges human works according to their thoughts,
until He judges His people’s case and gladdens them with His mercy.
Mercy is timely in the season of His people’s affliction, like rain clouds in a season without rain.
Have mercy on us, Master, God of all; look upon us and cast Thy fear upon all the nations.
Raise Thy hand against foreign nations, and let them see Thy dominion.
Just as Thou wast sanctified in us before them, so mayest Thou be magnified in them before us.
Let them know Thee, as we also have known that there is no God except Thee, Lord.
Renew signs and make wonders different; glorify Thy hand and right arm.
Rouse anger and pour out wrath; remove the adversary and destroy the enemy.
Hasten the time and remember the oath, and let them recount Thy mighty deeds.
Let the survivor be consumed in fiery wrath, and let those who harm Thy people find destruction.
Crush the heads of enemy rulers who say, “There is no one except us.”
Gather all the tribes of Jacob, and give them their inheritance as from the beginning.
Have mercy, Lord, on the people called by Thy name, and on Israel, whom Thou didst liken to a firstborn.
Have compassion on the city of Thy sanctuary, Jerusalem, the place of Thy rest.
Fill Zion with the recounting of Thine excellence, and Thy people with Thy glory.
Give testimony to those Thou didst create in the beginning, and raise up the prophecies spoken in Thy name.
Give a reward to those who wait for Thee, and let Thy prophets be found trustworthy.
Hear, Lord, the petition of Thy supplicants, according to Aaron’s blessing concerning Thy people,
and all those upon the earth will know that Thou art Lord, the God of the ages.
The belly will eat every food, yet one food is better than another.
The throat tastes food from the hunt; so an understanding heart tastes false words.
A twisted heart will give grief, and a person of much experience will repay it.
A woman will accept any male, yet one daughter is better than another.
A woman’s beauty gladdens the face and surpasses every human desire.
If mercy and gentleness are upon her tongue, her husband is unlike ordinary human sons.
The one who acquires a wife begins a possession: a helper corresponding to him and a pillar of rest.
Where there is no fence, property will be plundered; where there is no wife, a wanderer will groan.
For who will trust a well-girded robber springing from city to city?
So it is with a person who has no nest and lodges wherever evening overtakes him.
Every friend will say, “I too have shown friendship,” but there is a friend who is a friend in name alone.
Is there not grief to the point of death when a companion and friend turns to enmity?
O evil thought, from where did you roll in to cover the dry land with deceit?
A companion enjoys his friend’s gladness but will stand against him in a time of affliction.
A companion labors with a friend for his belly’s sake; before battle he will take up a shield.
Do not forget a friend in your soul or be unmindful of him in your wealth.
Every counselor exalts counsel, but there is someone who counsels for himself.
Guard your soul against a counselor, and know beforehand what he needs—for he too will counsel for himself—lest he cast a lot against you
and say to you, “Your road is good,” then stand opposite to see what happens to you.
Do not take counsel with someone who looks suspiciously at you, and hide your counsel from those who envy you.

Do not consult a woman about her rival, a coward about war, a merchant about exchange, a buyer about selling, a grudging person about gratitude, a merciless person about kindness, a lazy person about any work, a yearly hired worker about completing it, or an idle household slave about much labor. Do not rely on these for any counsel.
Instead, remain with a godly man whom you know to keep commandments, whose soul is in accord with your soul, and who will share your pain if you stumble.
Establish the counsel of your heart, for you have nothing more trustworthy than it.
For a man’s soul is sometimes accustomed to report more than seven watchmen seated high upon a watchtower.
Besides all these things, petition the Most High to make your road straight in truth.
A word is the beginning of every work, and counsel precedes every action.
The trace of a heart’s change brings forth four parts:
good and evil, life and death; the tongue continually rules them.
There is a skillful man who instructs many, yet is useless to his own soul.
There is someone who displays wisdom in words but is hated; this person will lack all food,
for grace was not given him from the Lord, because he was deprived of all wisdom.
There is someone wise for his own soul, and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy upon his mouth.
A wise man will instruct his own people, and the fruits of his understanding are trustworthy.
A wise man will be filled with blessing, and all who see him will call him happy.
A man’s life is a number of days, but Israel’s days are beyond numbering.
The wise person will inherit trust among his people, and his name will live for ever.
Child, in your life test your soul; see what is bad for it and do not give it that.
For not everything benefits everyone, and not every soul takes pleasure in everything.
Do not be insatiable in every luxury, and do not abandon yourself to dishes of food.
For with much food there will be illness, and insatiability will approach the point of bilious vomiting.
Many have died through insatiability, but the one who takes care will add life.
Honor a physician with his due honors, according to the need for him; for the Lord created him also.
For healing is from the Most High, and the physician will receive a gift from a king.
A physician’s knowledge will raise his head, and he will be admired before dignitaries.
The Lord created medicines from the earth, and a prudent man will not reject them.
Was not water sweetened by wood, so that its strength might be known?
He Himself gave human beings knowledge, to be glorified in His wonderful works.
By these He healed and removed the sufferer’s pain; with these a perfumer will make a mixture,
and His works will certainly not come to an end; from Him there is peace upon the face of the earth.
Child, do not be negligent in your illness, but pray to the Lord, and He Himself will heal you.
Put wrongdoing away, straighten your hands, and cleanse your heart from every sin.
Give a fragrant offering and a memorial of fine flour, and make your offering rich, as one who is no more.
Give the physician a place too, for the Lord created him; do not let him leave you, for you need him.
There is a time when success is also in their hands,
for they themselves will petition the Lord to grant them success in relief and healing for the sake of preserving life.
May the one who sins before his Maker fall into a physician’s hands.
Child, shed tears over the dead and begin a lament as one suffering terribly. Lay out his body according to his due, and do not neglect his burial.
Make your weeping bitter and your lament fervent; mourn according to his worth for one day or two because of slander, and be comforted because of grief.
For death comes from grief, and grief of heart will bend strength.
In calamity grief also remains, and the poor person’s life weighs upon the heart.
Do not give your heart over to grief; put it away, remembering the last things.
Do not forget: there is no return. You will not benefit this person, and you will harm yourself.
“Remember my judgment, for yours is likewise: yesterday for me, today for you.”
When the dead person rests, bring his remembrance to rest, and be comforted concerning him when his spirit departs.
A scribe’s wisdom comes through the opportunity of leisure; the one whose activity is reduced will become wise.
How will someone become wise who holds a plow, boasts in a goad’s shaft, drives oxen, is occupied with their work, and whose talk is about the offspring of bulls?
He will give his heart to making furrows, and his wakefulness to fodder for heifers.

So also every craftsman and master-builder who spends the night like the day, those who engrave signet engravings: his persistence is in varying the design. He will give his heart to making the depiction lifelike, and his wakefulness to finishing the work.

So also a smith sitting near an anvil and studying works of iron: the fire’s vapor will melt his flesh, and he will struggle in the furnace’s heat. He will incline his ear to the hammer’s sound, and his eyes are upon the pattern of the vessel. He will give his heart to completing works, and his wakefulness to finishing their adornment.
So also a potter sitting at his work and turning a wheel with his feet, who is continually anxious over his work, and whose whole labor is measured by number.
With his arm he will shape clay, and before his feet he will bend his strength. He will give his heart to completing the coating, and his wakefulness to cleaning the kiln.
All these trusted in their hands, and each shows skill in his own work.
Without them a city will not be settled, and people will neither sojourn nor walk about.
Yet they will not be sought for the people’s council or rise high in the assembly; they will not sit on a judge’s chair or consider a covenant of judgment.
They will certainly not make instruction and judgment known or be found among proverbs, but they will sustain the fabric of the world, and their petition is in the work of their craft.
Different is the one who gives his soul to considering the law of the Most High: he will seek out the wisdom of all the ancients and occupy himself with prophecies.
He will preserve the discourse of renowned men and enter into the turns of parables.
He will seek out the hidden meanings of proverbs and dwell among the riddles of parables.
He will serve among dignitaries and appear before rulers. He will pass through the land of foreign nations, for he has experienced good and evil among human beings.
He will give his heart to rising early before the Lord his Maker and petition the Most High. He will open his mouth in prayer and petition concerning his sins.
If the great Lord is willing, he will be filled with a spirit of understanding. He himself will rain down words of his wisdom and give thanks to the Lord in prayer.
He will direct his counsel and knowledge rightly and consider His hidden things.
He will reveal the instruction of his teaching and boast in the law of the Lord’s covenant.
Many will praise his understanding, and it will not be erased for ever. His memory will not depart, and his name will live for generations of generations.
Nations will recount his wisdom, and the assembly will proclaim his praise.
If he remains, he will leave a name greater than a thousand; if he rests, it suffices for him.
Having reflected further, I will recount more, for I have become full like the moon at midmonth.
Listen to me, holy sons, and sprout like a rose growing beside a flowing stream.
Give a fragrant scent like frankincense, and blossom like a lily. Spread a scent and offer a song of praise; bless the Lord for all His works.
Ascribe greatness to His name and give thanks with His praise, with songs of lips and lyres; and thus you will say in thanksgiving:
“All the Lord’s works are very good, and every command will come to pass at its time. One cannot say, ‘What is this? What is this for?’ For everything will be sought at its time.
At His word water stood like a heap, and at the utterance of His mouth came reservoirs of water.
In His command is all His good pleasure, and no one can diminish His salvation.
The works of all flesh are before Him, and nothing can be hidden from His eyes.
From age to age He has looked upon everything, and nothing is astonishing before Him.
One cannot say, ‘What is this? What is this for?’ For all things have been created for their uses.
His blessing covered like a river and drenched dry land like a flood.
So nations will inherit His wrath, as when He turned waters into brine.
His ways are straight for the holy, but likewise stumbling blocks for the lawless.
Good things were created for the good from the beginning, and likewise evil things for sinners.
The first necessities for human life are water, fire, iron, salt, fine wheat flour, milk, honey, the blood of the grape, oil, and clothing.
All these are good for the godly, but likewise will turn into evils for sinners.
There are spirits created for retribution; in His anger He made their scourges firm. At the time of completion they will pour out strength and assuage their Maker’s anger.
Fire, hail, famine, and death—all these were created for retribution;
the teeth of beasts, scorpions, vipers, and a sword exacting retribution upon the ungodly to their destruction.
They will rejoice in His command and be prepared upon the earth for their uses; at their times they will not transgress His word.”
Therefore from the beginning I stood firm, reflected, and left this in writing:
“All the Lord’s works are good, and He will supply every need at its proper hour.
One cannot say, ‘This is worse than that,’ for everything will prove good at its time.”
And now sing hymns with all your heart and mouth, and bless the Lord’s name.

Give a fragrant scent like frankincense, and blossom like a lily. Spread a scent and offer a song of praise; bless the Lord for all His works.
Ascribe greatness to His name and give thanks with His praise, with songs of lips and lyres; and thus you will say in thanksgiving:
“All the Lord’s works are very good, and every command will come to pass at its time. One cannot say, ‘What is this? What is this for?’ For everything will be sought at its time.
At His word water stood like a heap, and at the utterance of His mouth came reservoirs of water.
In His command is all His good pleasure, and no one can diminish His salvation.
The works of all flesh are before Him, and nothing can be hidden from His eyes.
From age to age He has looked upon everything, and nothing is astonishing before Him.
One cannot say, ‘What is this? What is this for?’ For all things have been created for their uses.
His blessing covered like a river and drenched dry land like a flood.
So nations will inherit His wrath, as when He turned waters into brine.
His ways are straight for the holy, but likewise stumbling blocks for the lawless.
Good things were created for the good from the beginning, and likewise evil things for sinners.
The first necessities for human life are water, fire, iron, salt, fine wheat flour, milk, honey, the blood of the grape, oil, and clothing.
All these are good for the godly, but likewise will turn into evils for sinners.
There are spirits created for retribution; in His anger He made their scourges firm. At the time of completion they will pour out strength and assuage their Maker’s anger.
Fire, hail, famine, and death—all these were created for retribution;
the teeth of beasts, scorpions, vipers, and a sword exacting retribution upon the ungodly to their destruction.
They will rejoice in His command and be prepared upon the earth for their uses; at their times they will not transgress His word.”
Therefore from the beginning I stood firm, reflected, and left this in writing:
“All the Lord’s works are good, and He will supply every need at its proper hour.
One cannot say, ‘This is worse than that,’ for everything will prove good at its time.”
And now sing hymns with all your heart and mouth, and bless the Lord’s name.
Do not be hasty with your mouth, and do not let your heart hurry to bring out a word before God, for God is in heaven and you are on earth. Therefore let your words be few.
For a dream comes with much distraction, and a fool’s voice with many words.
Whenever you vow a vow to God, do not delay paying it, for there is no delight in fools. Pay whatever you vow.
Better that you do not vow than that you vow and do not pay.
Do not let your mouth cause your flesh to sin, and do not say before God, “It was ignorance,” lest God become angry at your voice and destroy the works of your hands.
For with many dreams come futilities and many words; therefore fear God.
Ask the Lord for rain in its season, early and late. The Lord made appearances and will give them winter rain, to each person vegetation in the field.

For those making pronouncements spoke troubles, the diviners false visions; they were telling false dreams and giving vain comfort. Therefore they were carried away like sheep and mistreated, because there was no healing.
My wrath was provoked against the shepherds, and I will attend to the lambs. The Lord God Almighty will attend to His flock, Judah’s house, and make them like His splendid horse in battle.
“For a mortal born of woman is short-lived and full of wrath.
Like a flower that blossomed, he fell away; he fled like a shadow and will not remain.
Didst Thou not take account of this one also, and bring him into judgment before Thee?
For who will be clean from filth? No one.
Even if his life on earth is one day, his months are numbered with Thee; Thou didst set a time, and he will certainly not go beyond it.
And when you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you, you shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.
There shall not be found among you one who purifies his son or his daughter by fire, or practises divination, or interprets spoken omens, or observes auguries, or works sorcery,
or chants spells, or is a medium, or observes portents, or inquires of the dead.
For everyone who does these things is an abomination unto the Lord your God; for because of these abominations the Lord shall destroy them from before you.
You shall be perfect before the Lord your God.
For these nations whose possession you inherit hearken unto omens and divinations; but the Lord your God has not granted you so to do.
And He said unto them: Hear My words: If there is a prophet among you unto the Lord, I will make Myself known unto him in a vision, and I will speak unto him in sleep.
Not so My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.
I will speak unto him mouth to mouth, in visible appearance, and not through riddles; and he saw the glory of the Lord. And why were you not afraid to speak against My servant Moses?
I heard what the prophets speak, the false things they prophesy in My name, saying, I dreamed a dream.
How long will it be in the heart of the prophets prophesying false things, and in their prophesying the wishes of their own heart?
They plan to forget My law through their dreams, which each told his neighbor, just as their fathers forgot My name through Baal.
Let the prophet in whom there is a dream tell his dream, and the one to whom My word comes tell My word in truth. What has chaff to do with wheat? So are My words, says the Lord.
Are not My words like blazing fire, says the Lord, and like an axe cutting rock?
Therefore behold, I am against the prophets, says the Lord God, who steal My words, each from his neighbor.
Behold, I am against the prophets who cast out prophecies of the tongue and doze their own dozing.

Behold, I am against the prophets who prophesy false dreams, who told them and led My people astray by their lies and wanderings. I did not send or command them, and they will bring this people no benefit at all.
Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish, but to fulfil.
For truly I tell you: until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota nor one stroke shall pass from the Law, until all things come to pass.
Thirteen: Mēm. How I loved Thy law, Lord! It is my meditation all day.
Thou madest me wiser than my enemies in Thy commandment, for it is mine for ever.
I understood more than all who teach me, for Thy testimonies are my meditation.
I understood more than elders, for I sought Thy commandments.
I restrained my feet from every evil way, so that I might keep Thy words.
I did not turn away from Thy judgments, for Thou didst instruct me.
How sweet are Thy sayings to my throat, beyond honey and honeycomb to my mouth!
From Thy commandments I gained understanding; therefore I hated every way of injustice, for Thou didst instruct me.
For we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of our affliction that occurred in Asia: we were burdened far beyond our strength, so that we despaired even of living.
Indeed, we ourselves had the sentence of death within us, so that we might rely not on ourselves but on God who raises the dead.
He delivered us from so great a death and will deliver us; in Him we have set our hope that He will deliver us yet again,
Behold, the Lord’s eyes are upon those who fear Him, those who hope in His mercy,
to rescue their souls from death and nourish them in famine.
Our soul waits for the Lord, for He is our helper and defender.
For our heart will rejoice in Him, and we have hoped in His holy name.
May Thy mercy, Lord, be upon us, just as we have hoped in Thee.
Of David, before being anointed. The Lord is my light and my Savior; whom will I fear? The Lord is the protector of my life; of whom will I be afraid?
When those doing evil approached me to eat my flesh, those who afflict me and my enemies, they grew weak and fell.
Even if an army draws up against me, my heart will not fear; even if war rises against me, in this I hope.
Hallelujah! Blessed is the man who fears the Lord; he will greatly delight in His commandments.
His seed will be powerful in the land; a generation of the upright will be blessed.
Glory and riches are in his house, and his righteousness remains for an age of an age.
Light sprang up in darkness for the upright— merciful, compassionate and righteous.
Kind is the man who has compassion and lends; he will manage his words with judgment.
For he will never be shaken; the righteous person will be an everlasting memorial.
He will not fear an evil report; his heart is ready to hope in the Lord.
His heart is established; he shall certainly not fear, until he looks upon his enemies.
Do not give your foot over to shaking, and may your Keeper not slumber.
Behold, the One guarding Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
The Lord will guard you; the Lord is your shelter at your right hand.
By day the sun will not scorch you, nor the moon by night.
The Lord will guard you from all evil; He will guard your soul.
The Lord will guard your coming in and your going out, from now and for ever.

He will come, and it will be: a cloud will shade every place of Mount Zion and everything around her by day, and as of smoke and as of a light of fire burning by night; with all the glory it will be covered.
It will be shade from heat, shelter and concealment from harshness and rain.
Now to Him who is able to guard you from stumbling and to make you stand blameless before His glory with exultation,
to the only God our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, might, and authority before all time, and now, and into all the ages. Amen.
Of David. Bless the Lord, my soul, and all that is within me, His holy name.
Bless the Lord, my soul, and do not forget all His repayments:
who is gracious toward all your lawless deeds, who heals all your diseases;
who redeems your life from corruption, who crowns you with mercy and compassions;
who fills your desire with good things; your youth will be renewed like an eagle’s.
The sacrifices of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, but the prayers of those going straight are acceptable to Him.
The ways of the impious are an abomination to the Lord, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.
“What is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” says the Lord. “I am full of burnt offerings of rams; fat of lambs and blood of bulls and male goats I do not desire,
not even if you come to appear before Me. For who demanded these things from your hands? To trample My court,
you will no longer continue. If you bring fine flour, it is futile. Incense is an abomination to Me. Your new moons and sabbaths and a great day I cannot endure; fasting and idleness,
and your new moons and your festivals My soul hates. You have become more than enough for Me; I will no longer let your sins go.
Whenever you stretch your hands toward Me, I will turn My eyes away from you. Even if you multiply supplication, I will not listen to you, for your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves, become clean. Remove the evils from your souls, before My eyes. Stop your evil deeds.
Learn to do good, seek judgment, rescue the wronged. Give judgment for the orphan and vindicate the widow.
“For I am the Lord who loves righteousness and hates plunder obtained through injustice. I will give their labor’s yield to righteous people and make an everlasting covenant with them.
while the ungodly crossed a boundary, seizing a flock together with its shepherd?
They led away the orphans’ pack animal and took a widow’s cow as a pledge.
They diverted powerless people from a righteous road; together the meek of the earth hid.
They departed like donkeys in a field, going out beyond me to their own activity; bread became sweet to him for the young.
They harvested a field before its time, though it was not theirs; the powerless worked the ungodly’s vineyards without pay or food.
They made many lie down naked without garments and took away the covering of their lives.
They become wet from the mountain showers; because they have no shelter, they clasped a rock.
They snatched an orphan from the breast and humbled one who had fallen.
They unjustly made people lie down naked and took the morsel from the hungry.
They unjustly lay in ambush in narrow places and did not know a righteous road.
Come now, you rich people: weep and howl over the miseries coming upon you.
Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a testimony against you and will devour your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.
Look, the wages of the laborers who reaped your fields, withheld by you, cry out; and the cries of the harvesters have entered the ears of the Lord Sabaoth.
You lived luxuriously on the earth and indulged yourselves; you fattened your hearts on a day of slaughter.
You condemned; you murdered the righteous one. He does not oppose you.
You shall not wrong your neighbour, neither shall you rob; and the wages of the hired worker shall in no wise remain with you overnight until morning.
For all things there is a time, and a season for every matter beneath heaven.
a time to give birth and a time to die, a time to plant and a time to uproot what is planted,
a time to kill and a time to heal, a time to pull down and a time to build,
a time to weep and a time to laugh, a time to beat the breast in mourning and a time to dance,
a time to throw stones and a time to gather stones, a time to embrace and a time to keep far from embracing,
a time to seek and a time to lose, a time to keep and a time to throw away,
a time to tear and a time to sew, a time to be silent and a time to speak,
a time to love and a time to hate, a time of war and a time of peace.
Whosoever touches a dead person, any human being who has died, shall be unclean for seven days.
That person shall be purified on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. If he is not purified on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Whosoever touches the dead body of any human being who has died, and is not purified, has defiled the Tent of the Lord; that soul shall be wiped out from Israel. Because water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him, he is unclean; his uncleanness is still in him.

For if, after escaping the world’s defilements through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in them and overcome, their last state has become worse than their first.
For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment handed down to them.
What the true proverb says has happened to them: “A dog has returned to its own vomit,” and, “A sow, after washing, returns to wallowing in mud.”
saying, ‘Why did we fast, and Thou didst not see? We humbled our lives, and Thou didst not notice?’ For on your fasting days you pursue your wishes and prod all those under your control.
If you fast for lawsuits and fights and strike a humble person with fists, why do you fast for Me as today, to make your voice heard in an outcry?

I did not choose this fast, or a day for a person to humble his life. Even if you bend your neck like a ring and spread sackcloth and ashes beneath you, you will not thereby call it an acceptable fast.

‘It is not such a fast that I chose,’ says the Lord. ‘Instead, loosen every bond of injustice, undo the strangling ties of coercive agreements, release the crushed, and tear up every unjust written contract.
Break your bread for the hungry and bring homeless poor people into your house. If you see someone naked, clothe him; do not overlook those belonging to your own family.
Then your light will break out early, and your healings quickly rise. Your righteousness will go ahead of you, and God’s glory will enfold you.
Then you will cry, and God will hear you. While you are still speaking He will say, “Behold, I am present.” If you remove from yourself a bond, finger-pointing, and a word of grumbling,
In the days of His flesh, He offered petitions and supplications, with loud crying and tears, to the One able to save Him out of death, and was heard because of His reverent fear.
Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from the things He suffered,
and, having been perfected, He became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey Him,
But if, in seeking to be justified in Christ, we ourselves were also found to be sinners, is Christ then a servant of sin? May it never be!
For if I rebuild the things I tore down, I show myself to be a transgressor.
For through law I died to law, so that I might live to God. I have been crucified with Christ.
And I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself for me.
I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through law, then Christ died for nothing.”
With it we bless the Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings who have been made in God’s likeness.
From the same mouth come blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to happen this way.
Does a spring pour out sweet and bitter water from the same opening?
My brothers, can a fig tree produce olives, or a vine figs? Neither can salt water produce sweet water.
Saul said to Samuel, “Because I listened to the people’s voice. I went on the mission the Lord sent me on, brought Agag, Amalek’s king, and destroyed Amalek.
The people took flocks and cattle herds from the spoils, the first of what was marked for destruction, to sacrifice before the Lord our God at Gilgal.”
Samuel said, “Are whole burnt offerings and sacrifices as desirable to the Lord as listening to the Lord’s voice? Behold, obedience is better than sacrifice, and attentiveness than the fat of rams.
Divination is sin; teraphim bring sorrow and troubles. Because you treated the Lord’s word as nothing, the Lord will treat you as nothing, so that you will not be king over Israel.”
Therefore through Him let us continually offer God a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips confessing His name.
And do not forget to do good and to share, for God is pleased with such sacrifices.
Doing righteous things and speaking truth are more pleasing before God than the blood of sacrifices.
Three times a year you shall keep a feast to Me.

Keep the feast of unleavened bread; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of new grain; for in it you came out of Egypt. You shall not appear before Me empty-handed.

And you shall keep the feast of harvest, of the firstfruits of your labours which you sow in your field; and the feast of completion as the year goes out, when you gather your labours out of your field.
Every male of yours shall appear three times in the year before the Lord your God.
For when I cast out nations before you, and enlarge your borders, you shall not sacrifice the blood of My offering with leaven, neither shall the fat of My feast remain until morning.
You shall bring the firstfruits of the first produce of your land into the house of the Lord your God. You shall not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk.
And you Philippians also know that at the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no Church shared with me in the matter of giving and receiving except you alone,
because even in Thessalonica you sent once and twice for my need.
Not that I seek the gift, but I seek the fruit that increases to your account.
But I have received everything and have an abundance; I have been filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things from you, a fragrant aroma, an acceptable sacrifice, well pleasing to God.
And my God will fill every need of yours according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
In Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian,
devout and fearing God with his whole household, giving many alms to the people and praying to God continually.
About the ninth hour of the day, he clearly saw in a vision an angel of God come in to him and say, “Cornelius.”
He stared at him in fear and said, “What is it, sir?” The angel said to him, “Your prayers and your alms have ascended as a memorial before God.
Honor the Lord from your righteous labors, and offer Him firstfruits from your fruits of righteousness,
so that your storerooms may be filled with an abundance of grain and your vats gush with wine.
Now this is the point: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows in blessings will also reap in blessings.
Let each give as he has decided in his heart, not out of sorrow or compulsion; for God loves a cheerful giver.
And God is able to make every grace abound toward you, so that, always having all sufficiency in everything, you may abound in every good work.
As it is written, “He scattered abroad; he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains for the age.”
Now the One who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed and increase the fruits of your righteousness.
You are being enriched in everything for all generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us,

Three times in the year shall every male among you appear before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord shall choose: in the Feast of Unleavened Bread, and in the Feast of Weeks, and in the Feast of the Pitching of Tents. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty,
but every man according to the ability of your hands, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which He has given you.
One who has mercy on the poor lends to God, and He will repay him according to his gift.
For the Lord your God, He is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great and mighty and fearful God, who shows no partiality, neither takes a bribe;
who executes judgment for the sojourner, and the orphan, and the widow, and loves the sojourner, to give him bread and clothing.
Sing to God; make music to His name. Make a road for Him who rides upon the west—Lord is His name— and exult before Him. They will be troubled before Him,
the Father of orphans and judge of widows, God in His holy place.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
But if you afflict them, and they cry aloud to Me, I will surely listen to their voice,
I will be angry with wrath and kill you with the sword. Your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
And if you lend silver to your poor brother beside you, you shall not press him hard, neither shall you lay interest upon him.
The Lord’s eyes are upon the righteous, and His ears toward their supplication.
But the Lord’s face is against those who do evil, to destroy their remembrance from the earth.
The righteous cried out, and the Lord heard them; from all their afflictions He rescued them.
The Lord is near to the brokenhearted, and He will save the humble in spirit.
And He told them a parable about their need to pray always and not lose heart,
saying, “There was a certain judge in a certain city who neither feared God nor respected any person.
And there was a widow in that city who kept coming to him, saying, ‘Give me justice against my adversary.’
For a time he was unwilling. But afterward he said within himself, ‘Even though I do not fear God or respect any person,
yet because this widow troubles me, I will give her justice, lest by coming continually she wear me down.’”
And the Lord said, “Hear what the unrighteous judge says.
And will not God bring about justice for His chosen ones who cry to Him day and night? And will He delay over them?
I tell you, He will bring about justice for them speedily. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will He find faith on the earth?”
He also told this parable to some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and regarded the rest as nothing:
“Two men went up into the temple to pray, one a Pharisee and the other a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed these things to himself: ‘God, I thank Thee that I am not like the rest of humanity—plunderers, unrighteous people, adulterers—or even like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week; I tithe everything I acquire.’
But the tax collector, standing far away, would not even lift his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, the sinner.’
I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”
and you will take up this lament against Babylon’s king and say on that day, “How the one who made demands has rested, and the taskmaster rested!
God shattered the sinners’ yoke, the rulers’ yoke;
having struck a nation in wrath with an incurable blow, striking a nation with a blow of anger that did not spare,
But by your hardness and unrepentant heart, you store up wrath for yourself on the day of wrath and revelation of God’s righteous judgment,
who will repay each according to his works:
to those who, through perseverance in good work, seek glory and honor and incorruptibility, eternal life;
but to those acting from selfish ambition, who disobey the truth but obey unrighteousness, wrath and fury,
The heart is deep beyond all things, and so is a human; and who will know him?
I, the Lord, examine hearts and test kidneys, to give each according to his ways and the fruits of his practices.
In the day of vengeance I will repay, in the season when their foot shall slip; for the day of their destruction is near, and the things prepared for you are at hand.
For the Lord shall judge His people, and be moved concerning His servants; for He saw them weakened, and failing under assault, and exhausted.
“Let us go and return to the Lord our God, because He has seized us and will heal us; He will strike and dress our wounds.
He will restore us to health after two days; on the third day we will rise and live before Him.
We will know; we will pursue knowledge of the Lord. We will find Him ready like dawn, and He will come to us like rain, early and late upon the land.”
Pour out Thy wrath upon nations that do not know Thee, and upon kingdoms that did not call on Thy name,
for they devoured Jacob and made his place desolate.
Do not remember our ancient acts of lawlessness; let Thy compassions swiftly reach us first, for we became very poor.
Help us, God our Savior. For the glory of Thy name, Lord, rescue us, and be propitious toward our sins for Thy name’s sake,
Therefore say to Israel’s house, ‘Thus says the Lord: I am not acting for you, house of Israel, but because of My holy name, which you profaned among the nations where you entered.
I will sanctify My great name, profaned among the nations, which you profaned among them. The nations will know that I am the Lord when I am sanctified in you before their eyes.
I will take you out of the nations, gather you out of all the lands and bring you into your own land.
There is none like Thee among gods, Lord, and nothing is like Thy works.
All the nations Thou madest will come and bow down before Thee, Lord, and glorify Thy name,
for Thou art great and dost wondrous things; Thou alone art the great God.
And as in the days of your departure from Egypt, you will see wonderful things.
Nations will see and be ashamed of all their strength. They will place hands over their mouth; their ears will be deafened.
They will lick dust like snakes dragging along the earth; they will be thrown into turmoil in their confinement. They will be astonished at the Lord our God and fear Thee.
lest the nations say, “Where is their God?” And let vengeance for the poured-out blood of Thy servants be known among the nations before our eyes.
Let the groaning of those in bonds enter before Thee; according to the greatness of Thine arm, preserve the sons of those put to death.
Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom their insult with which they insulted Thee, Lord.
But we, Thy people and the sheep of Thy pasture, will give Thee thanks for ever; from generation to generation we will proclaim Thy praise.
Nevertheless God will crush His enemies’ heads, the crown of hair of those walking in their offenses.
The Lord said, “I will return from Bashan; I will return in the depths of the sea,
so that your foot may be dipped in blood, and the tongue of your dogs from enemies, from him.”
then the Lord shall heal your sins, and have mercy upon you, and shall gather you again from all the nations whither the Lord has scattered you.
If your dispersion is from one end of heaven unto the other end of heaven, from thence shall the Lord your God gather you, and from thence shall the Lord your God take you.
And the Lord your God shall bring you into the land which your fathers inherited, and you shall inherit it; and He shall do you good, and make you more numerous than your fathers.
And you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus says the Lord: Israel is My firstborn son.
And I said to you, “Let My people go, that they may serve Me.” If therefore you will not let them go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son.’”
For the Lord chose Zion; He selected her as His dwelling:
“This is My rest for age upon age; here I will dwell, for I selected her.
Shine, shine, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the Lord’s glory has risen upon you.
Behold, darkness and gloom will cover earth over nations, but the Lord will appear upon you, and His glory will be seen over you.
Kings will walk by your light, and nations by your radiance.
Thus says the Lord who redeems you and forms you from the womb: “I am the Lord who completes all things. I stretched heaven alone and established the earth. Who else
will scatter the signs of spirit-mediums and divinations from the heart, turning the discerning backward and making their counsel foolish,

and establish His servant’s words and make His messengers’ counsel true? He says to Jerusalem, ‘You will be inhabited,’ and to Judea’s cities, ‘You will be rebuilt,’ and her deserted places will spring up;

and kings will be your foster fathers and ruling women your nurses. They will bow to you upon the earth’s surface and lick the dust of your feet. You will know that I am the Lord, and you will not be ashamed.
For the end. Among hymns. A psalm of a song.
May God have compassion on us and bless us; may He make His face shine upon us. Diapsalma.
That Thy way may be known on earth, Thy salvation among all nations.
Let peoples give thanks unto Thee, God; let all peoples give thanks unto Thee.
Let nations rejoice and exult, for Thou wilt judge peoples in uprightness and guide nations upon the earth. Diapsalma.
Let peoples give thanks unto Thee, God; let all peoples give thanks unto Thee.
The earth gave its fruit; may God, our God, bless us.
May God bless us, and let all earth’s ends fear Him.
For the ear discerns words, and the throat tastes food.
And the Lord God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. Let Us make him a helper corresponding to him.”

And God also formed from the earth every wild beast of the field and every bird of heaven, and brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. And whatever Adam called each living creature, that was its name.
And Adam gave names to all the cattle, all the birds of heaven, and all the wild beasts of the field. But for Adam no helper like himself was found.
And God cast a deep sleep upon Adam, and he slept. And He took one of his ribs and filled its place with flesh.
And the Lord God fashioned the rib He had taken from Adam into a woman, and brought her to Adam.
And Adam said: This, at last, is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh. She shall be called Woman, for she was taken from her husband.
For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh.
She clothed herself in strength and dignity and rejoiced in the last days.
Let your fountain of water be your own, and share joy with the wife of your youth.

Let a deer of affection and a colt of your graces keep company with you. Let your own woman lead you and be with you at every time, for as you move in the company of her affection, you will be one among many.
As when a bird flies down from its own nest, so a person is enslaved when estranged from his own places.
For the poor will not be forgotten utterly; the endurance of the needy will not perish for ever.
See, see that I am, and there is no god beside Me. I will put to death, and make alive; I will smite, and I will heal; and there is none that shall deliver out of My hands.
For I will lift My hand unto heaven, and swear by My right hand, and say, I live for ever.
For I will sharpen My sword as lightning, and My hand shall lay hold of judgment; and I will repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Me will I repay.
I will make My arrows drunk with blood, and My sword shall devour flesh, from the blood of the slain and of captives, from the head of the rulers of the enemies.

Rejoice, O heavens, together with Him, and let all the sons of God worship Him; rejoice, O nations, with His people, and let all the angels of God give Him strength; for He avenges the blood of His sons, and shall avenge and repay a penalty unto the enemies, and unto them that hate Him shall He repay; and the Lord shall thoroughly cleanse the land of His people.
His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying,
“Blessed is the Lord, the God of Israel, because He has visited and accomplished redemption for His people,
and has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David His servant,
as He spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from long ago:
salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all who hate us,
to show mercy to our fathers and remember His holy covenant,
the oath He swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that, rescued from our enemies’ hand, we might serve Him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before Him all our days.
Now, Master, hear Thy servant’s prayer and my supplications. Let Thy face look upon Thy desolate holy mountain, for Thy servants’ sake, Master.

Attend with Thine ear, Lord, and hear me. Open Thine eyes and see our desolation and that of Thy city, over which Thy name has been called. For we make our supplication in our prayers before Thee because of Thy mercy, not our righteous deeds.
Lord, be propitious! Lord, hear and act, and do not delay, for Thine own sake, Master, because Thy name has been called over Thy city Zion and Thy people Israel.”
The Lord is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that will seek Him as good
and will endure and be quiet for the Lord’s salvation.
We treated Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us leave her; let each of us go to our own land, for her judgment reached heaven and rose to the stars.
The occupations of her houses are secure, and she did not eat idle food.
She opens her mouth wisely and according to law, and her mercy raised up her children, and they became wealthy, and her husband praised her:
“Many daughters acquired wealth, many did mighty things, but you stand above and have surpassed them all.”
A woman’s pleasing qualities are false and beauty is vain; for an understanding woman is blessed, and let her praise the fear of the Lord.
Do not be carried away by varied and strange teachings, for it is good for the heart to be strengthened by grace, not by foods, which have not benefited those occupied with them.
All things are permitted, but not all things are beneficial. All things are permitted, but not all things build up.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying: Thus you shall bless the sons of Israel, saying unto them (and they shall put My name upon the sons of Israel, and I, the Lord, will bless them):
The Lord bless you and keep you;
the Lord make His face shine upon you, and have mercy upon you;
the Lord lift up His face upon you, and give you peace.
May your hand be found by all your enemies; may your right hand find all who hate you.
You will make them like a fiery furnace at the time of your presence; the Lord in His anger will throw them into turmoil, and fire will devour them.
You will destroy their fruit from the earth and their seed from the sons of men,
Smoke rose in His anger, and fire from His face set things ablaze; coals were kindled from Him.
But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives to all generously and without reproach, and it will be given to him.
But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
For that person must not suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord,
a man of divided mind, unstable in all his ways.
Wealth adds many friends, but the poor person is abandoned even by the friend he has.
A false witness will not be unpunished, and one who accuses unjustly will not escape.
Many attend the faces of kings, but every evil person becomes a reproach to a man.

Everyone who hates a poor brother will also be far from friendship. A good thought will draw near to those who know it, and an intelligent man will find it. One who does many evils brings wickedness to completion, and one who provokes words will not be saved.
For if an enemy had reproached me, I would have endured it; and if the one hating me had boasted against me, I would have hidden from him.
But you, a man of like soul, my leader and my acquaintance,
you who made food sweet together with me: in God’s house we walked in concord.
Do not abandon your friend or an ancestral friend, and do not enter your brother’s house when misfortune strikes you; a nearby friend is better than a brother dwelling far away.
A weeping enemy agrees to everything with his lips, but in his heart devises deceits;
if the enemy entreats you with a loud voice, do not be persuaded, for seven evils are in his life.
One who hides enmity establishes deceit, but one well known in councils discloses his own sins.
The king instructed the elders who had stood before Solomon his father while he was still alive, saying, “How do you advise me, so that I may answer this people?”
They said to him, “If this day you become this people’s servant, serve them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants always.”
He abandoned the elders’ counsel which they had given him and consulted the young men who had been brought up with him and stood before him.
He said to them, “What do you advise, and what shall I answer this people who said to me, ‘Lighten the collar your father placed on us’?”

The young men who had been brought up with him and stood before him said, “Thus speak to this people who told you, ‘Your father made our collar heavy; now lighten it for us.’ Thus speak to them: ‘My little part is thicker than my father’s loins.
Now my father burdened you with a heavy collar, but I will add to your collar. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.’”
One who walks with the wise will be wise, but one who walks with fools will be known.
A man’s heart is perceptive; his life is sorrowful, but when he rejoices, he does not mingle with insolence.
Make Thy mercy heard by me in the morning, for I hoped in Thee. Make known to me, Lord, the way I shall walk, for unto Thee I lifted my soul.
Take me out from my enemies, Lord, for I fled unto Thee for refuge.
Teach me to do Thy will, for Thou art my God. Thy good Spirit will lead me on level ground.
Death and life are in the hand of the tongue, and those who control it will eat its fruits.
But if you bear the name Jew, and rest upon law and boast in God,
and know His will and approve the things that matter, being instructed from the law,
and are confident that you yourself are a guide of the blind, a light to those in darkness,
an instructor of the senseless, a teacher of infants, having in the law the embodiment of knowledge and truth—
you then who teach another, do you not teach yourself? You who proclaim that one must not steal, do you steal?
You who say that one must not commit adultery, do you commit adultery? You who abhor idols, do you rob temples?
You who boast in law, do you dishonor God through transgression of the law?
From fruits of a mouth a man’s life will be filled with good things, and the recompense of his lips will be given to him.
The lips of the righteous know lofty things, but fools die in want.
The days of our years—in them are seventy years, or, with strength, eighty years; the greater part of them is toil and pain, for gentleness came upon us, and we shall be disciplined.
Who knows the might of Thine anger, and Thy wrath from the fear of Thee?
So make known how to number Thy right hand, and those bound in heart in wisdom.
I will destroy Moab, says the Lord, as he goes up to an altar and burns incense to his gods.
Therefore my heart, Moab, will hum like flutes; my heart will hum like a flute for Kiradas’s people. Therefore what he acquired perished from a person.
They will shave every head in every place; every beard will be shaved, all hands will beat themselves, and on every waist is sackcloth.
If you sit to dine at the table of rulers, thoughtfully consider what is set before you,
and lay your hand to it, knowing that you must prepare such things;
but if you are more insatiable, do not desire his foods, for these belong to a false life.
Having found honey, eat what is sufficient, lest you become full and vomit.
All things are permitted to me, but not all things are beneficial. All things are permitted to me, but I will not be brought under the authority of anything.
A gentle-tempered man is a physician of the heart, but a perceptive heart is a moth to the bones.
Nevertheless, hear the Lord’s word that I speak in your ears and in all the people’s ears:
The prophets who were before me and before you from of old prophesied over much land and against great kingdoms concerning war.
The prophet who prophesied peace—when the word comes, they will know the prophet whom the Lord sent to them in faithfulness.
Foods are for the stomach, and the stomach for foods, but God will bring both it and them to an end. Yet the body is not for sexual immorality but for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.
A sweet voice will multiply its friends, and a well-spoken tongue will multiply friendly greetings.
Let those at peace with you be many, but your counselors one out of a thousand.
If you acquire a friend, acquire him through testing, and do not trust him quickly.
For there is a friend for his own occasion who will certainly not remain on the day of your affliction.
There is also a friend who turns to enmity and will expose a quarrel to your reproach.
There is also a friend who shares your tables but will certainly not remain on the day of your affliction.
In your prosperity he will be like you, and he will speak freely to your household slaves;
if you are brought low, he will be against you and hide from your face.
Separate yourself from your enemies, and be cautious with your friends.
A faithful friend is a strong shelter; and whoever has found him has found a treasure.
There is no exchange for a faithful friend, and no weight to measure his excellence.
A faithful friend is medicine for life, and those who fear the Lord will find him.
The one who fears the Lord will guide his friendship rightly, for as he is, so also is his neighbor.

Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road to the gate. Whenever a man with a case came before the king for judgment, Absalom called to him, “What city are you from?” The man would answer, “Your servant is from one of Israel’s tribes.”
Absalom would say to him, “Your claims are good and straightforward, but no one from the king is here to hear you.”
Absalom would say, “Who will appoint me judge in the land, so that every man with a dispute or case will come to me and I will give him justice?”
Whenever a man approached to bow down to him, Absalom would stretch out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him warmly.
Absalom did this to all Israel who came to the king for judgment. Absalom made the hearts of the men of Israel his own.
At the end of forty years, Absalom said to his father, “Please let me go to Hebron and fulfill the vows I made to the Lord.
Your servant made a vow while I was living at Geshur in Syria: ‘If the Lord indeed brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the Lord.’”
The king said to him, “Go in peace.” He rose and went to Hebron.
Absalom sent spies throughout all Israel’s tribes, saying, “When you hear the horn’s sound, say, ‘King Absalom has begun to reign in Hebron!’”
Two hundred invited men went with Absalom from Jerusalem. They went in their simplicity and knew nothing of the matter.
While sacrificing, Absalom sent and summoned Ahithophel the Gelmonite, David’s counselor, from his city Gola. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.
Behold, I have set before your face this day life and death, good and evil.

If you obey the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His ordinances and His judgments, then you shall live and be many; and the Lord your God shall bless you in all the land into which you go to inherit it.
And if your heart turns aside, and you will not hearken, and you are led astray to bow down unto other gods and serve them,
I declare unto you this day that you shall surely perish, and you shall in no wise be long-lived upon the land which the Lord your God gives you, into which you are crossing the Jordan to inherit it.
I call heaven and earth to witness unto you this day: I have set before your face life and death, the blessing and the curse. Choose life, that you and your seed may live,
Blessed is the person who found wisdom, the mortal who saw good sense,
for trading in her is better than treasures of gold and silver.
She is more valuable than costly stones; nothing evil will stand against her. She is readily known to all who approach her, and nothing precious is worthy of her.
For length of life and years of living are in her right hand, and wealth and glory in her left.
Righteousness proceeds from her mouth, and she carries law and mercy on her tongue.
Her ways are good ways, and all her paths are in peace.
She is a tree of life to all who hold her fast, and secure for those who lean on her as on the Lord.
Do not walk after your desires, and restrain your appetites.
If you supply your soul with the satisfaction of desire, it will make you an object of your enemies’ gloating.
Do not rejoice in great luxury, lest you be bound to contribute to it.
Do not become poor by feasting on borrowed money when you have nothing in your purse.
How sufficient a little is for an instructed person! He does not pant upon his bed.
Healthy sleep comes with a moderate stomach. He rose early, and his soul was with him. The pain of sleeplessness, bilious vomiting, and cramp accompany an insatiable man.
If you have been forced to eat too much, rise, vomit at a distance, and you will find rest.
If the heaven is raised to the height, says the Lord, and the earth’s ground lowered beneath, even then I do not reject Israel’s family, says the Lord, for all they did.
Thus said the Lord, who gave the sun for daylight, moon and stars for night light, and a cry in the sea so its waves boomed—the Lord Almighty is His name:
If these laws cease from before Me, says the Lord, then Israel’s family will cease to be a nation before Me for all days.
Moses led the sons of Israel onward from the Red Sea and brought them into the wilderness of Shur. They travelled three days in the wilderness without finding water to drink.
They came to Marah but could not drink its water because it was bitter. Therefore that place was named Bitterness.
The people murmured against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”

And Moses cried to the Lord; and the Lord showed him a piece of wood, and he cast it into the water, and the water was made sweet. There He appointed ordinances and judgments for him, and there He tested him,

and said, “If you diligently listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and do what is pleasing before Him, and give ear to His commandments, and keep all His ordinances, I will bring upon you none of the diseases which I brought upon the Egyptians; for I am the Lord who heals you.”

In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. Isaiah son of Amos the prophet came to him and said, ‘Thus says the Lord: Give instructions for your house, for you are dying and shall not live.’
Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord,
‘I pray Thee, Lord, remember how I walked before Thee in truth and with a full heart, and did what was good in Thine eyes.’ Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Isaiah was in the middle courtyard when the Lord’s word came to him:

‘Return and tell Hezekiah, leader of My people: Thus says the Lord, the God of your father David: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Behold, I shall heal you; on the third day you shall go up to the Lord’s house,
and I shall add fifteen years to your days. I shall save you and this city from the hand of the king of the Assyrians, and shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.’
He said, ‘Let them take a cake of figs and place it on the ulcer, and he will recover.’
After this He went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and said to him, “Follow Me.”
Leaving everything, he rose and followed Him.
Levi gave a great reception for Him in his house. A large crowd of tax collectors and others was reclining with them.
The Pharisees and their scribes grumbled to His disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are ill do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
Luke, the beloved physician, greets you, and Demas.
A perceptive man, keen in his works, must stand beside kings and not stand beside sluggish men.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take spices: five hundred shekels of the choicest myrrh, half as much fragrant cinnamon, two hundred and fifty, and two hundred and fifty of fragrant cane,
five hundred sanctuary shekels of iris, and a hin of olive oil.
Make these into holy anointing oil, a compound prepared by a perfumer’s skill. It shall be holy anointing oil.
The Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
“Behold, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with a divine Spirit of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in every kind of work,
to plan and design, to work in gold, silver, bronze, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and spun fine linen,
to work in stone and the woodworking crafts, and to perform every kind of work.
Is anyone among you suffering? Let him pray. Is anyone cheerful? Let him sing praise.
Is anyone among you sick? Let him summon the elders of the Church, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the Lord’s name.
And the prayer of faith will save the weary sick person, and the Lord will raise him up; and if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.
Therefore confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, so that you may be healed. A righteous person’s petition has great strength when it is at work.
Submit yourselves therefore to God; but resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, sinners, and purify your hearts, you of divided mind.
Be wretched and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into mourning and your joy into dejection.
Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.
And if a soul brings a gift as a sacrifice unto the Lord, his gift shall be fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense upon it. It is a sacrifice.

And he shall bring it unto the sons of Aaron, the priests; and when he has taken from it a full handful of the fine flour with the oil and all its frankincense, the priest shall place its memorial portion upon the altar: a sacrifice, a sweet savour unto the Lord.
And what remains of the sacrifice shall be Aaron’s and his sons’; it is most holy among the sacrifices of the Lord.
And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant Thy servants to speak Thy word with all boldness,
while Thou stretchest out Thy hand for healing, and signs and wonders take place through the name of Thy holy Servant Jesus.”
When they had prayed, the place where they were gathered was shaken. They were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke God’s word with boldness.
And the life of Sarah was a hundred and twenty-seven years.
And Sarah died in the city of Arbok, which is in the hollow, that is, Hebron, in the land of Canaan; and Abraham came to lament Sarah and to mourn.
And Abraham rose up from his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying,
“I am a resident foreigner and a sojourner among you. So give me a possession for burial among you, that I may bury my dead away from me.”
And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan; and they lamented him with a great and exceedingly grievous lamentation, and he mourned his father seven days.
A rejoicing heart makes one flourish, but a sorrowful man’s bones dry up.
Do not give your soul over to grief, and do not afflict yourself with your deliberation.
Gladness of heart is a person’s life, and a man’s rejoicing is length of days.
Beguile your soul, comfort your heart, and put grief far from you; for grief has destroyed many, and there is no benefit in it.
Jealousy and anger shorten days, and anxiety brings old age before its time.
David understood that his servants were whispering and perceived that the child had died. David said to his servants, “Has the child died?” They said, “He has died.”

David rose from the ground, washed, anointed himself, and changed his clothes. He entered God’s house and bowed down to Him. Then he entered his own house and asked for bread to eat; they set bread before him, and he ate.
His servants said to him, “What is this that you have done? While the child was still alive, you fasted and wept and kept vigil, but when the child died, you rose and ate bread and drank.”
David said, “While the child was still alive, I fasted and wept, because I said, ‘Who knows whether the Lord will have mercy on me and the child will live?’
But now he has died. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”
For I set all this upon my heart, and my heart saw all this: the righteous, the wise and their works are in God’s hand. A person knows neither love nor hatred; everything lies before them.

There is futility in everything: one event comes to the righteous and the ungodly, to the good and the bad, to the clean and the unclean, to the one who sacrifices and the one who does not sacrifice. As the good person, so the sinner; as the one who swears, so the one who fears an oath.

This is an evil in all that is done under the sun: one event comes to everyone. Moreover, the heart of human beings is full of evil, and delirium is in their heart during their lives; afterward they go to the dead.
You shall take two emerald stones and engrave the names of the sons of Israel on them,
six names on one stone and the six remaining names on the other, according to their generations.
With a stoneworker’s craftsmanship, like a seal engraving, you shall engrave the two stones with the names of the sons of Israel.

You shall place the two stones on the shoulders of the shoulder-piece. They are memorial stones for the sons of Israel, and Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on his two shoulders before the Lord as a memorial concerning them.
Behold, I am creating you, not like a smith blowing coals and bringing out an implement for work. I did not create you for ruin, to destroy
For a craftsman sharpened iron, worked it with an adze, bored it with a drill, and worked it with his strong arm. He will hunger and grow weak and certainly not drink water. Having selected
The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, saying:
Rise and go down to the potter’s house, and there you will hear My words.
And I went down to the potter’s house, and behold, he was doing work upon the stones.
And the vessel he was making fell apart in his hands, and again he made it another vessel, as pleased him to make.
And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:
Can I not shape you as this potter does, house of Israel? Behold, you are like the potter’s clay in My hands.

For a potter, laboriously kneading soft earth, shapes each object for our service; from the same clay he fashioned alike vessels serving clean purposes and those serving the opposite; and the clay-worker decides the use of each kind.

With evil labor he also shapes a futile god from the same clay, though he himself, having come from earth a little before, will shortly go back to that from which he was taken, when the debt of his soul is demanded.
Moses said to the sons of Israel, “Behold, God has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the divine Spirit of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge of all things,
to design in every craft, working gold, silver, and bronze,
to work stone and shape wood, and to carry out every work of skill.
He has put it in his mind to teach—both him and Eliab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with wisdom and understanding of mind to comprehend and do all the work of the sanctuary: weaving and embroidering in scarlet and fine linen, carrying out every work of design and embroidery.”
The land’s surplus is in everything—a king of a cultivated field.
Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, and did not stand in the way of sinners, and did not sit in the seat of pestilent men;
but his will is in the Lord’s law, and on His law he will meditate day and night.
He will be like the tree planted beside the outlets of waters, which will give its fruit in its season, and whose leaf will not fall off; and everything he does will be prospered.
Of understanding. Of Asaph. Attend, my people, to my law; bend your ear to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter riddles from the beginning,
whatever we heard and knew, and our fathers recounted to us,
it was not hidden from their children for another generation, as we announce the Lord’s praises, His mighty acts and the wonders He did.
The proverbs of Solomon son of David, who reigned in Israel,
for knowing wisdom and discipline and understanding words of good sense,
for receiving turns of speech, understanding true righteousness, and directing judgment rightly,
so that he may give shrewdness to the innocent, perception and thought to a young child.
For a wise person who hears these things will become wiser, and the discerning will acquire guidance,
and understand a comparison and an obscure saying, the utterances of the wise and riddles.

The fear of God is the beginning of wisdom, and good understanding belongs to all who practice it. Reverence toward God is the beginning of perception, but the ungodly will despise wisdom and discipline.
The Lord gave the young men knowledge, understanding, and practical wisdom in every literary skill; to Daniel He gave understanding in every utterance, vision, dreams, and all wisdom.
After these days the king ordered them brought in, and the chief eunuch brought them before King Nebuchadnezzar.
The king conversed with them, and among the wise no one was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. They remained beside the king.

In every matter of discourse, understanding, and education about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times wiser than the learned experts and philosophers throughout his kingdom. The king honored them, appointed them rulers, and declared them wiser than all his own men in affairs throughout his land and kingdom.
Give ear to my words, Lord; understand my cry.
Attend to the voice of my petition, my King and my God, for unto Thee I will pray, Lord.
In the morning Thou wilt hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before Thee and watch.
To each is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the common benefit.
For to one a word of wisdom is given through the Spirit, and to another a word of knowledge according to the same Spirit;
to another faith in the same Spirit, and to another gifts of healings in the one Spirit;
to another acts of power, to another prophecy, to another discernments of spirits, to another kinds of tongues, and to another interpretation of tongues.
But the one and the same Spirit works all these things, distributing to each individually just as He wills.
Then, in a vision that very night, the king’s mystery was plainly revealed to Daniel. Daniel blessed the Lord Most High,
and cried out, “The name of the great Lord will be blessed for ever, because wisdom and majesty belong to Him.
He changes seasons and times, transfers kings and appoints them, gives wisdom to the wise and understanding to those who possess knowledge,
reveals deep and dark things, knows what is in darkness and what is in light, and with Him is a dwelling.
To Thee, Lord of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, because Thou hast given me wisdom and prudence. Now Thou hast shown me everything I requested, to disclose these things to the king.”
Blessed art Thou, Lord; teach me Thine ordinances.
With my lips I declared all the judgments of Thy mouth.
In the way of Thy testimonies I delighted, as in all wealth.
I will ponder Thy commandments and consider Thy ways.
I will meditate on Thine ordinances; I will not forget Thy words.
The memory of righteous people is with praises, but the name of the impious is extinguished.
