The queen of Sheba heard Solomon’s name and the Lord’s name, and came to test him with riddles.
She came to Jerusalem with a very great retinue, with camels carrying spices, very much gold, and precious stones. She came in to Solomon and spoke to him about everything in her heart.
Solomon explained all her matters to her. No matter was overlooked by the king that he did not explain to her.
When the queen of Sheba saw all Solomon’s discernment and the house he had built,
Solomon’s food, the seating of his attendants, the station of his ministers, his clothing, his wine-pourers, and his whole burnt offering which he offered in the Lord’s house, she was beside herself.
She said to King Solomon, “The report I heard in my land about your word and your discernment is true.
I did not believe those speaking to me until I arrived and my eyes saw. Behold, it is not half as they reported to me! You have added good things beyond them, beyond every report I heard in my land.
Blessed are your women! Blessed are these attendants of yours who stand before you continually, hearing all your discernment!

Blessed be the Lord your God, who delighted in you, setting you on Israel’s throne! Because the Lord loves Israel, to establish them for ever, He made you king over them to carry out judgment in righteousness and in their judgments.”
I will heal their dwellings; I will love them openly, because My anger turned away from them.
I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like a lily and put down his roots like Lebanon.
His branches will spread, and he will be like an olive tree laden with fruit; his fragrance will be like Lebanon.
They will return and settle beneath his shelter; they will live and be filled to intoxication with grain. His memorial will blossom like a vine, like Lebanon’s wine.
As for Ephraim, what has he still to do with idols? I humbled him, and I will strengthen him. I am like a thickly shading juniper; from Me your fruit is found.
Shout to God, all the earth; sing and exult and make music.
Make music to the Lord with a lyre, with a lyre and the sound of a psalm.
With hammered trumpets and the sound of a horn trumpet, shout before the King, the Lord.
And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good. And there was evening, and there was morning: a sixth day.
What surplus does the worker gain from the things for which he toils?
I saw the distraction God has given human beings to be distracted by.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also put the age in their hearts, so that human beings may not find out the work God has done from beginning to end.
I knew that there is no good for them except to rejoice and do good during one’s life.
Moreover, whenever a person eats and drinks and sees good in all his toil, this is God’s gift.
I knew that everything God has done will endure for ever. Nothing can be added to it, and nothing taken from it; God has done this so that people may fear before Him.
Thy right hand, O Lord, has been glorified in strength; Thy right hand, O Lord, has shattered enemies.
And in the abundance of Thy glory Thou didst shatter Thine adversaries; Thou didst send forth Thy wrath, and it devoured them as stubble.
And by the breath of Thy wrath the water parted; the waters stood fast as a wall; the waves stood fast in the midst of the sea.
The enemy said, ‘I will pursue and overtake; I will divide the spoil; I will fill my soul; I will slay with my sword; my hand shall have dominion.’
Thou didst send forth Thy wind, and the sea covered them; they sank as lead in mighty waters.
The people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, and the priests lifted up the ark of the covenant of the Lord ahead of the people.

As the priests carrying the ark of the covenant entered the Jordan and the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord dipped into the edge of the Jordan’s water—the Jordan was overflowing its whole bank, as in the days of wheat harvest—

the waters coming down from above stood. One mass stood very, very far away, as far as the region of Kiriath-jearim. The water flowing down descended into the Sea of Arabah, the Salt Sea, until it failed completely. The people stood opposite Jericho.

The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All the sons of Israel crossed on dry ground until the whole people had finished crossing the Jordan.
For I knew that the Lord is great, and our Lord is above all the gods.
Everything the Lord willed, He did, in heaven and on earth, in the seas and all the deeps.
He brings clouds up from the earth’s extremity; He made lightning for rain; He brings winds out of His treasuries.
From heaven the Lord looked down; He saw all the sons of men.
From His prepared dwelling place He looked upon all who inhabit the earth.
He formed their hearts individually; He understands all their deeds.
For the end. A psalm for David. Lord, Thou didst test me and know me.
Thou knewest my sitting and my rising; Thou didst understand my reasonings from afar.
Thou didst trace my path and my measuring cord, and Thou didst foresee all my ways.
For there is no word on my tongue,
behold, Lord, Thou knewest all things, the last and the first; Thou didst form me and place Thy hand upon me.
Thy knowledge was made wondrous beyond me; it grew strong—I cannot reach it.
Remember the former things from eternity, for I am God, and there is none besides Me,
announcing the last things beforehand, before they came to be—and together they were fulfilled. I said, ‘All My counsel will stand, and I will do everything I have planned,’
Thus says the Lord who rescued you, Israel’s Holy One: “I am your God. I have shown you how to find the road on which you will walk.
If you had listened to My commands, your peace would have become like a river and your righteousness like a sea wave.
Your offspring would have become like sand, those born from your belly like the earth’s dust. Even now you will certainly not be destroyed, nor will your name perish before Me.”
He made rivers a wilderness and outlets of waters thirst,
a fruitful land brine, because of the wickedness of those inhabiting it.
He made a wilderness lakes of waters and waterless land outlets of waters,
and settled hungry people there, and they established a city of habitation,
and sowed fields and planted vineyards and produced a fruitful crop.
He blessed them, and they multiplied greatly, and He did not diminish their livestock.
Who is wise and will understand these things, or discerning and will recognize them? For the Lord’s ways are straight; the righteous will walk in them, but the impious will grow weak in them.

And it shall be, when you pass over the Jordan into the land which the Lord your God gives you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that the Lord your God shall set you above all the nations of the earth.
And all these blessings shall come upon you, and find you, if you diligently hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God.
Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field.
Blessed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Blessed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out.
The Lord your God deliver your enemies who rise against you, crushed before your face. By one way shall they come out against you, and by seven ways shall they flee before you.
The Lord send His blessing upon you in your storerooms, and in all that you put your hand unto, upon the land which the Lord your God gives you.

And it shall be, if you do not hearken unto the voice of the Lord your God, to keep and do all His commandments which I command you this day, that all these curses shall come upon you, and overtake you.
Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field.
Cursed are your storehouses and your reserves.
Cursed are the offspring of your womb, and the produce of your land, the herds of your cattle, and the flocks of your sheep.
Cursed are you when you go out, and cursed are you when you come in.

The Lord send upon you want, and famine, and wasting, in all that you put your hand unto, whatsoever you do, until He destroys you, and causes you to perish speedily, because of your evil practices, because you have forsaken Me.
The Lord make death cleave unto you, until He consumes you from the land whither you go to inherit it.
The Lord smite you with destitution, and fever, and chills, and inflammation, and slaughter, and wind blight, and pallor; and they shall pursue you until they destroy you.
And the heaven above your head shall be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron.
The Lord give dust for the rain of your land; and earth shall descend upon you from heaven, until He wears you away, and until He destroys you.
He makes His angels winds, and His ministers a burning fire.
I will gather evils against them, and spend My arrows upon them.

They shall waste away with hunger, and be devoured by birds, and suffer incurable backward-bending spasms; I will send against them the teeth of wild beasts, with the fury of things that crawl upon the ground.
Without, the sword shall bereave them; and from the inner chambers, terror: the young man together with the maiden, the nursing child with the aged elder.
Praise the Lord from the earth, dragons and all deeps,
fire, hail, snow, ice, storm wind—all fulfilling His word,
All wait for Thee to give them food at the right time.
When Thou givest to them, they will gather; when Thou openest Thy hand, all things will be filled with goodness.
For God did not make death, neither does He delight in the destruction of the living.
For He created all things that they might exist, and the created things of the world are life-preserving; there is no poison of destruction in them, nor is Hades’ dominion upon the earth.
For righteousness is immortal.
For creation, serving Thee who made it, strains itself for punishment against the unrighteous and relaxes itself for benefit on behalf of those who trust in Thee.
Therefore at that time also, changing into all things, it served Thy gift that nourishes all, according to the desire of those in need,
so that Thy sons whom Thou didst love, Lord, might learn that it is not the production of fruits that nourishes a human being, but Thine utterance that preserves those who trust in Thee.
For the Lord your God brings you into a good and spacious land, where are torrents of water and springs of the depths, flowing through the plains and through the hills;
a land of wheat and barley, vines, fig trees, and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,
a land wherein you shall eat your bread without poverty, and shall lack nothing; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you shall mine copper.
And you shall eat and be filled, and bless the Lord your God upon the good land which He has given you.
And the Lord said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward heaven, and there shall be hail throughout all the land of Egypt, upon men, and upon livestock, and upon every plant upon the earth.”
Moses stretched out his hand toward heaven. The Lord sent thunder and hail, and fire ran over the earth. The Lord rained hail upon all the land of Egypt.
There was hail, with fire flaming amid the hail. The hail was very, very abundant, such as had never been in Egypt since a nation came to be there.
Throughout Egypt the hail struck people and livestock. It struck every plant in the plains and shattered all the trees there.
Only in the land of Goshen, where the sons of Israel were, was there no hail.
Besides becoming wise, Ecclesiastes also taught the people knowledge; and an ear will trace out an orderly arrangement of proverbs.
Ecclesiastes sought much to find words of delight and something written in uprightness, words of truth.
They call the wise and understanding worthless, but those sweet in speech will hear more.
All who fashion and carve are futile, making what pleases them, things that will not help them. But they will be ashamed—
all who fashion a god and carve useless things,
and all from whom they came have dried up. Let the deaf from among humankind all assemble and stand together; let them be abashed and ashamed together.
wood, a craftsman set it by measure and arranged it with glue. He made it like a man’s form and human beauty, to set it in a house.
The wood he cut from the woodland was what the Lord planted and rain made grow,
Behold, newcomers will approach you through Me and take refuge with you.

every perishable implement. I will not grant success against you. Every voice will rise against you in judgment; you will defeat them all, and those accountable to you will be held liable in it. There is an inheritance for those serving the Lord, and you will be righteous before Me,” says the Lord.
One who trusts in a rash heart is a fool; but one who walks in wisdom will be saved.
Give ear and hear my voice; pay attention and hear my words.
Will the plowman plow all day? Or will he prepare seed before working the ground?
When he has leveled its surface, does he not then sow a little black cumin and cumin, and again sow wheat, barley and emmer within your borders?
You will be disciplined by your God’s judgment and will rejoice.
For black cumin is not cleaned with harshness, nor will a wagon wheel roll over cumin; black cumin is shaken out with a rod, but cumin
will be eaten with bread. For I will not be angry with you for ever, nor will the sound of My bitterness trample you.
These wonders too came from the Lord Sabaoth. Take counsel; raise up futile consolation!

“For from the sun’s rising to its setting, My name has been glorified among the nations, and in every place incense is brought to My name, together with a pure sacrifice, because My name is great among the nations,” says the Lord Almighty.
“But you profane it by your saying, ‘The Lord’s table is polluted, and the foods placed upon it are despised.’

“And you said, ‘These things are from hardship,’ and I blew them away,” says the Lord Almighty. “You were bringing things seized by force, the lame and the afflicted. If you bring the sacrifice, shall I accept these things from your hands?” says the Lord Almighty.

“Cursed is one who was able, and had a male in his flock and a vow concerning it, yet sacrifices a damaged animal to the Lord. For I am a great King,” says the Lord Almighty, “and My name is manifest among the nations.”
If the lawless person turns from all the lawlessness he committed, keeps all My commandments, and practices righteousness and mercy, he will surely live; he certainly will not die.
None of the transgressions he committed will be remembered. By the righteousness he practiced, he will live.
Do I at all desire the death of the lawless, says the Lord, rather than his turning from his evil way and living?
You shall surely tithe all the produce of your seed, the yield of your field, year by year.

And you shall eat it before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there. You shall bring the tithes of your grain, and of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and of your sheep, that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.

And if the way is too long for you, so that you cannot carry them, because the place which the Lord your God shall choose for His name to be called upon there is far from you, when the Lord your God has blessed you,
then you shall sell them for silver, and take the silver in your hands, and go unto the place which the Lord your God shall choose.

And you shall spend the silver for whatsoever your soul desires, for cattle, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever your soul desires; and you shall eat there before the Lord your God, and rejoice, you and your house,
This too I saw as wisdom under the sun, and it seemed great to me:
There was a small city with few people in it; a great king might come against it, surround it and build great siegeworks against it,
and he might find in it a poor wise man, who will deliver the city by his wisdom; yet no one remembered that poor man.
I said, Wisdom is better than strength; yet the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard.
The words of the wise, heard quietly, are better than the shouting of rulers in follies.
Wisdom is better than weapons of war, but one sinner will destroy much good.
A good name is more desirable than much wealth, and good favor is above silver and gold.
For the end. A psalm of David.
Lord, the king will rejoice in Thy power and exult greatly in Thy salvation.
Thou gavest him the desire of his soul and didst not deprive him of the wish of his lips. Diapsalma.
For Thou didst meet him with blessings of kindness; Thou didst place upon his head a crown of precious stone.
He asked Thee for life, and Thou gavest it to him, length of days for the age of the age.
His glory is great in Thy salvation; Thou wilt bestow glory and magnificence upon him.
For Thou wilt give him blessing for the age of the age; Thou wilt gladden him with joy in Thy presence.
For the king hopes in the Lord, and through the Most High’s mercy he will certainly not be shaken.
And Joseph fell upon his father’s face, and wept over him, and kissed him.
And Joseph commanded his servants the embalmers to prepare his father for burial; and the embalmers prepared Israel for burial.
And they fulfilled forty days for him, for this is how the days of burial preparation are reckoned; and Egypt mourned him seventy days.
And when the days of mourning had passed, Joseph spoke to Pharaoh’s rulers, saying, “If I have found grace in your sight, speak concerning me in Pharaoh’s ears, saying,
“‘My father made me swear, saying, “In the tomb which I dug for myself in the land of Canaan, there you shall bury me.” Now therefore I will go up and bury my father, and return.’”
And Pharaoh said, “Go up and bury your father, as he made you swear.”
And Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all Pharaoh’s servants, and the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt,
and all Joseph’s household, and his brothers, and all his father’s house; but they left their kindred and their sheep and their oxen in the land of Goshen.
And chariots and horsemen also went up with him, and the company was exceedingly great.

And the inhabitants of the land of Canaan saw the mourning at the threshing floor of Atad, and said, “This is a great mourning for the Egyptians.” Therefore its name was called Mourning of Egypt, which is beyond the Jordan.
After their release, they went to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and elders had said to them.
On hearing it, they lifted their voice together to God and said, “Master, Thou art the One who made heaven and earth and the sea and everything in them,
who through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of our father David, Thy servant, said, ‘Why did nations rage and peoples devise empty things?
The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against His Christ.’
For truly, in this city, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, gathered against Thy holy Servant Jesus, whom Thou didst anoint,
to do whatever Thy hand and Thy purpose had determined beforehand should happen.
And the Lord spoke unto Moses, saying:
Speak unto the sons of Israel, and you shall say unto them: If a man or woman solemnly vows a vow of consecration unto the Lord, to be set apart

from wine and strong drink, he shall be purified from wine. He shall drink neither vinegar of wine, nor vinegar of strong drink, nor anything prepared from grapes; and he shall eat neither fresh grapes nor raisins.
All the days of his vow he shall consume nothing made from the vine: wine, from pressed grape skins unto the seed.
All the days of the vow of purification no razor shall come upon his head. Until the days which he vowed unto the Lord are fulfilled, he shall be holy, letting the hair of his head grow long.
All the days of his vow unto the Lord he shall not enter where any dead person is.
For his father, or his mother, or his brother, or his sister, he shall not defile himself when they die; for the vow of his God is upon him, upon his head.
All the days of his vow he shall be holy unto the Lord.
But if anyone dies suddenly beside him, the head of his vow shall be defiled forthwith. He shall shave his head on the day when he is cleansed; on the seventh day it shall be shaved.
And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons unto the priest, at the doors of the Tent of Testimony.

And the priest shall prepare one for sin and one for a whole burnt offering. And the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin in connection with the dead person, and shall consecrate his head on that day,

whereon he was consecrated unto the Lord for the days of the vow. And he shall bring a year-old lamb for a guilt offering; and the former days shall not be reckoned, for the head of his vow was defiled.
And this is the law of him who has vowed: on the day when he fulfils the days of his vow, he shall present his offering at the doors of the Tent of Testimony,
and he shall bring his gift unto the Lord: one unblemished year-old male lamb for whole burning, and one unblemished year-old ewe lamb for sin, and one unblemished ram for deliverance,
and a basket of unleavened bread of fine flour, loaves prepared with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, and their sacrifice and their drink offering.
And the priest shall present them before the Lord, and prepare his offering for sin and his whole burnt offering.
And he shall prepare the ram as a sacrifice of deliverance unto the Lord, with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest shall prepare its sacrifice and its drink offering.
And he who has vowed shall shave the head of his vow at the doors of the Tent of Testimony, and put the hair upon the fire which is under the sacrifice of deliverance.

And the priest shall take the boiled foreleg from the ram, and one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them upon the hands of him who has vowed, after he has shaved the hair of his vow.

And the priest shall bring them as a presentation before the Lord. It shall be holy unto the priest, with the breast of presentation and the foreleg of the portion set apart; and afterward he who has vowed shall drink wine.

This is the law of him who vows unto the Lord, his gift unto the Lord concerning the vow, apart from whatever his hand may find, according to the extent of his vow which he vows under the law of consecration.
My words have been spoken by God, an oracle concerning a king whom his mother instructed.
What will you keep, child? What? God’s sayings. Firstborn, I speak to you, son. What, child of my womb? What, child of my vows?
Do not give women your wealth, or your mind and livelihood to belated counsel.
Do everything with counsel; drink wine with counsel. The powerful are hot-tempered, but let them not drink wine,
so that, after drinking, they may not forget wisdom and become entirely unable to judge the weak rightly.
Give intoxicating drink to those in grief, and wine to drink to those in pain,
so that they may forget their poverty and no longer remember their troubles.
Open your mouth for God’s word, and judge everyone soundly.
Open your mouth and judge justly, and decide the case of the poor and weak.
A courageous woman—who will find her? Such a woman is more precious than costly stones.
Her husband’s heart is confident in her; such a woman will not lack fine spoils.
For she works good things for her husband throughout her life.
Spinning wool and flax, she made useful work with her hands.
She became like a ship trading from afar, and she gathers her livelihood.
And she rises in the night and gave food to the household and tasks to the maidservants.
After inspecting a farm she bought it, and from the fruits of her hands she planted an estate.
Having girded her waist strongly, she braced her arms for work.
She tasted that working is good, and her lamp is not extinguished throughout the night.
She stretches her forearms toward profitable things, and braces her hands on a spindle.
She opened her hands to a needy person and stretched out her wrist to a poor person.
Her husband is not anxious about those at home when he stays away somewhere, for all those with her are clothed.
She made double cloaks for her husband, and garments of fine linen and purple for herself.
Her husband becomes distinguished in the gates when he sits in council with the elder inhabitants of the land.
She made linen cloths and sold them, and girdles for the Canaanites.
She opened her mouth attentively and lawfully and prescribed order for her tongue.
Give her from the fruits of her hands, and let her husband be praised in the gates.
How great Thy works have become, Lord! Thou madest all things in wisdom; the earth was filled with Thy possession.
Here is the sea, great and spacious; there are creeping things without number, living creatures small with great.
There ships pass, and this dragon, which Thou didst form to play with it.
When Thou turnest Thy face away, they will be troubled. Thou wilt take back their breath, and they will fail and return to their dust.
Thou wilt send Thy Spirit, and they will be created, and Thou wilt renew the face of the earth.
Then Job replied:
“So you are the people! Surely wisdom will die with you!
I too have a heart like yours.
For a righteous and blameless man became an object of mockery.
For at an appointed time he was prepared to fall beneath others, and for his houses to be plundered by the lawless.
But indeed, let no wicked person trust that he will be innocent, nor those who provoke the Lord suppose that there will be no examination of them.
But ask the four-footed animals, to see whether they will tell you, and the birds of heaven, to see whether they will report to you.
Speak fully to the earth, to see whether it will tell you; and the fish of the sea will explain to you.
Who among all these did not know that the Lord’s hand made these things?
Is not the life of all living things in His hand, and the breath of every human being?
Then Job replied:
“Indeed, I know that the reproof is from my own hand, and His hand has become heavy upon my groaning.
Who, then, might know that I could find Him and come to an end?
